name: Community Chest Biodiversity Grants
summary: Grants from a district council for community groups and parish or town councils to plant native trees, hedgerows and wildflower meadows, put up bird and bat boxes, and create or improve wildlife habitat in South Cambridgeshire.

amount.note: Maximum award in any single financial year, can cover 100% of project costs

reporting: An end-of-project evaluation is due within three months of the project's completion.

steps: Application, by the 7th of a month

eligibility.rule: Project meets local need and leaves a legacy for the community
Project has support from all local District Councillors for the relevant wards
Not for ongoing revenue costs, past activities, fetes or fundraising events, or replacing other public funding
Project delivers a sustainable increase in local biodiversity
Biodiversity planting uses native trees, hedgerows, wildflower meadows or other vegetation
If previously funded by the Council, all monitoring and evaluation reports were submitted and found satisfactory

documents: Quote for the community activity or project
Correspondence from local District Councillors showing project support
Bank statement for the payment account
Plan of proposed biodiversity work, including project map and outcomes
Timeline of proposed work indicating mileposts and delivery date
Public Rights of Way consent from landowner, if relevant

applicant_types.quote: Biodiversity Grants (currently closed for applications) Who can apply: Community Group (including Community Interest Companies) Parish/Town Council of any size

geography.quote: This includes Community Interest Companies, (CIC) based in South Cambridgeshire or benefiting South Cambridgeshire residents.

access.quote: Apply for a Community Chest Grant

amount.quote: The maximum award is £2,000 in any single financial year (April to March) and can be for 100% of project costs.

co_finance_required.quote: Where appropriate, applicants are encouraged to seek part-funding from other sources including their Parish/Town council. There is no requirement for this

reporting.quote: an end of project evaluation must be submitted to us within 3-months of project completion

effort.quote: Applications must be received by the seventh day of any given month to be considered at the GAC meeting scheduled within that same month.
Grant applications are discussed at the Grants Advisory Committee.

eligibility.quote: meet local need and leave a legacy for the community
projects that have not received the support of all local District Councillor(s) for the ward/s concerned.

ongoing revenue costs or overheads (e.g. salaries, rent, advertising, promotional materials). activities, events or services which have already taken place, including staff development time. village fetes and fundraising events (one off or regular) projects that replace funding by other public sector bodies, including Parish/Town councils (for example youth services, highways)
the project must deliver a sustainable increase in local biodiversity, known as Biodiversity Net Gain.
planting of trees, hedgerows, wildflower meadows or other vegetation must be native.

Organisations that have previously received grant funding from the Council must have submitted all required monitoring and evaluation reports relating to earlier awards, and these reports must be deemed satisfactory by Council officers, before any new grant application will be considered by the GAC.

after_award.quote: an end of project evaluation must be submitted to us within 3-months of project completion

documents.quote: a copy of your organisation's constitution or mission statement a copy of your latest accounts (audited if available) a quote for the community activity or project a copy of your safeguarding policy a copy of any correspondence from your local District Councillor(s) showing they are supportive of your project a bank statement for the account you wish the funds to be paid into.

a plan of the proposed work, including a project map and project outcomes a timeline of the proposed work indicating mileposts and delivery date a brief management plan which describes how the project will be sustainable
public Rights of Way consent from landowner
